area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a bungalow, a ranch and a new build
area.scope.1.why: Park Ridge's older brick houses can still run boilers and radiators; post-war ranches run furnaces.
area.scope.2.why: Radiator-heated houses have no ducts for central air, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits.
area.scope.3.why: Houses rebuilt on older lots often run two systems, one per floor, so a repair starts with finding which one failed.
area.scope.4.why: Older houses keep the boiler or furnace in the basement; many ranches keep the furnace in a utility room.
area.scope.5.why: Shops around Uptown and the Metra stop run rooftop units or small furnaces, so opening hours set the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Park Ridge building
area.buildings.1.title: Brick Georgian or bungalow
area.buildings.1.body: Often a boiler and radiators, sometimes converted to forced air. Ductless is a common way to cool.
area.buildings.2.title: Post-war ranch
area.buildings.2.body: A furnace with central air, in the basement or a utility room. The condenser sits beside the house.
area.buildings.3.title: New house on an old lot
area.buildings.3.body: Two furnaces and AC systems, one per floor, with condensers beside the house.
area.buildings.4.title: Uptown shop
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units or a furnace for the shops around Uptown and the Metra stop.

area.faq.heading: Park Ridge HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Is the boiler in my older Park Ridge house worth repairing, or does it need replacing?
area.faq.2.q: Do you come out to Park Ridge from Chicago?
area.faq.3.q: Can you cool an older brick house without ductwork?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC work in Park Ridge need a permit?
area.faq.1.a: Often it's worth repairing. We diagnose first, and where the boiler has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.cta.body: Have the make of your boiler, furnace or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In a rebuilt house with two systems, tell us which floor has the problem.

buildingTypeOptions: New house on an old lot
extras.faq.2.a: Yes. Park Ridge is on our service area list, about 10 miles north-west of the shop at 1225 N Cleaver St, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Usually, yes. Radiator-heated houses have no ducts for central air, so cooling means ductless mini-splits, with the condenser beside the house.
extras.faq.4.a: It depends on the job. The City of Park Ridge sets its own permit rules, mostly for installs and replacements. A repair or tune-up is a different job. Ask whoever quotes an install who pulls the permit.
